segments: Cycle 28.
Arab Kings, as is fitting:
The Khilatians, the leaders of the factions,
who are called in the language of the country "mangdabrir", sprang
upon the partisans of Awhad,
and drove them out of the city,
and made war on the fortress.
And when Awhad heard [this],
he came and encamped against Khilat together with the forces of Mesopotamia.
And division fell among the citizens,
and Awhad gained control over it.
And he killed a great number of the Khilatians,
and many of them he bound and sent to Mayperqat (Mayyafariqin).
And the power of the young men, the leaders of the factions, was brought to naught,
those who according to their will used to set up rulers and depose [them].
And in that same year died Sultan Ghiyath al-Din Kaykhusraw,
and his son 'Izz al-Din Kayka'us became king.
And he seized his brother 'Ala' al-Din Kayqubad,
and sent [and] imprisoned him in the fortress of Masara, which is below the monastery of Mar Aaron on the Blessed Mountain, which is beside Melitene.
And in that same year the Franks went out from Tripoli,
and encamped against Homs,
and devastated its territory.
And its master, Asad al-Din Shirkuh, son of Muhammad, son of Shirkuh the Elder, had no strength
to drive them back.
And the Cypriots also captured many ships of the Tayyaye (Muslims),
and took them captive.
And when 'Adil heard, he went out from Egypt with armies,
and the Franks withdrew.
And in that same year died 'Ala' al-Din, son of Qara Sunqur, the lord of Maragha,
and after him succeeded a little son whom he had;
and after a little while he also died.
And Nusrat al-Din Abu Bakr, son of Pahlawan, the lord of Tabriz, came
and took control over Maragha and all its domain,
except for the fortress of Rawanduz,
in which rebelled the eunuch who had been the tutor of the boy who died.
And in the year 1520 [of the Greeks],
605 of the Tayyaye (Arabs/Muslims):
A great host of the Iberians (Georgians) went out and came to the territory of Khilat.
And they entered the city of Arjish,
and conquered it and plundered it,
and killed its old men and its young men,
and took captive the women and the boys and the girls.
And they destroyed it completely,
and left it ruined and plundered.
And Najm al-Din Awhad was in Khilat,
and he was unable to go out to meet them on account of their great numbers,
and because he did not trust the Khilatians because of the slaughter he had wrought among them,
lest, when he went out,
they should rebel and surrender it to the Iberians.
And in that same year there was a violent earthquake...
